text:
I work on the block so I am here pretty often. It's a Food Court McDonald's so the bar is already pretty low and I have come to terms with that being part of the arrangement on convenience.

But there is only so long you can line up and just accept that you will get what you get.

I've noticed in the last several months, they have prompted their cashiers to start peppering the customers with questions. Are you collecting points with the app? NO. How many ketchups do you want? NONE. How many napkins? TWO. I don't blame the cashiers, I don't think they have a choice, but now, asking me what type of pop I am going to get? What difference does it make? You are handing me an empty cup, you can press whatever button you want, it doesn't matter. Unless you are going to come around and fill it up for me, you don't need to know. I might take one shot of each of the pops, I might eat the cup, who knows!

The straw that broke the camel's back for me was tonight though. I have had too many warm cokes because they can't keep the ice machine running. I'm standing there, like an idiot, pressing my cup against the handle waiting for ice and nothing. I asked the supervisor if they have anything back there, ice in a jug, crushed ice, anything that would save me from a warm drink. NOPE, apparently they have to truck the ice in from across the food court somewhere and she needs to find someone to go get it.

What a mess. This place was already circling the drain on service, but now I can't even depend on them for ice. I suppose this is a positive for me, I'll put in more steps walking somewhere else.
author: Jim McDonald

text: Went to pick up my mobile takeout order and was handed off a tray, I asked the order to-go and the woman looked at me with a sneer in her face and told me that I didn't "punch in" a bag, oh, I didn't know that you need to pay for a paper bag in Mcdonald's nowadays. You got me right there girl, I am happy that I made your day with the amount of proud and provocation I saw in that face you were making we almost looked at each other for a good minute as if you were expecting me to make a fool of myself for that paper bag. I am sure you will do just as good in the macdonald's of your home nation when your student visa expires, keep up the good work!

text:
Worst McDonalds experience. I get that it’s quantity over quality and sometimes thing up under the radar, but this place wasn’t busy when I ordered. Every item had an issue.

My coffees were cold. Thankfully I caught it and they replaced them. My western bbq burger (having a great one the other day, and knowing the standard) looked like -and tasted- like a child had put it together. I counted half a strip of bacon on my McDouble add bacon. My fries were frozen and soggy.

I know the reality of the quality of McDonald’s. I eat it when I feel like trash, and want to continue feeling like trash.

But this?... come on.
